name: X-ray diffraction by crystals
description: Friedrich and Knipping, following Laue’s proposal, observed X-ray diffraction by crystals, opening a route to structural analysis.

impact.note: A laboratory result used by one profession, yet crystallography in chemistry, mineralogy, biology and materials all rest on it; scores imply tier 0.

date.basis: Year of the dated publication, or a broad historian-estimated composition interval; no first discovery claimed.

events.statement: A signed contemporary note records the Munich group’s work on X-ray interference from April 1912.

evidence.supports: Forman discusses the Munich experiment and notes that the contemporary memorandum states the work began on 21 April, without proving that was the date of the first successful diffraction pattern.
